label: Late input phase ramp leading up to <DEL>
explanation: Fires only in the input phase and on the delimiter: never at t=0-1, and almost never in the copy phase (0.1% of mass). Firing rate climbs with position, from 24% at t=2 to 84% at orig_idx 8, and reaches 75% on <DEL>, which holds 28% of the mass. Within a sequence the activation ramps up step by step and peaks at or near <DEL>; the top examples (~0.9-1.0 of max) are 9-token sequences. The ramp is weaker or gated off on digit inputs, on q, and on repeated tokens (in_first=0 rate 6% vs 39%), and sequences heavy in digits or repeats stay low. Adding these exclusions did not clearly beat the simple position rule (F1 0.72-0.73 vs 0.74). Many steps late in the input phase stay inactive in sequences without a clear token cause, so precision is about 0.69. The feature reads as a growing count of distinct letters seen so far that saturates toward the delimiter.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: w, i, e, r, m, j; least: -, f, q, p) and the input two steps back (most: i, w, r, e, j, m; least: f, p, q, -); timing cues that raise it most: phase=1, recall_idx=0, L=3 & t=5.
